```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Birhanu 2020 studied whether the plant phenolic **methyl gallate** (MG) changes
the pharmacokinetics of the veterinary fluoroquinolone **marbofloxacin** (MAR)
in rats, and how the combination's plasma kills *Salmonella* Typhimurium
*ex vivo*. Ten rats received 5 mg/kg MAR alone or with 20 mg/kg MG,
intravenously and orally, in a four-way crossover. Plasma from the orally dosed
rats was then incubated with *S.* Typhimurium for 24 h, and the change in
bacterial count was related to the sample's AUC0-24/MIC by a sigmoid Imax
model.

The authors fitted every quantity separately for the two treatments, so the
package carries one file per treatment. Each file holds the one-compartment
marbofloxacin PK and the *ex vivo* effect of a plasma sample drawn at any time.

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0234211>

```{r models}
mods <- c("Birhanu_2020_marbofloxacin_rat", "Birhanu_2020_marbofloxacin_methylGallate_rat")
uis <- lapply(mods, function(m) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m)))
names(uis) <- mods
cat(uis[[1]]$reference, "\n")
```

| Model file | Treatment | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Birhanu_2020_marbofloxacin_rat` | MAR 5 mg/kg alone | Tables 2-5, Figures 2-4 |
| `Birhanu_2020_marbofloxacin_methylGallate_rat` | MAR 5 mg/kg + MG 20 mg/kg | Tables 2-5, Figures 2-4 |

```{r descriptions, results = "asis"}
for (m in mods) cat("**", m, "** -- ", uis[[m]]$description, "\n\n", sep = "")
```

# Population

Ten clinically healthy male Sprague-Dawley rats (OrientBio, Korea), five weeks
old on arrival, acclimated for a week, weighing 180-215 g. Each rat received a
single 5 mg/kg MAR dose alone or with 20 mg/kg MG, intravenously or orally, in a
four-way crossover with two-week washouts. Tail-vein blood was taken at 0,
0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12 and 24 h and marbofloxacin measured by HPLC-UV
(LOQ 0.16 ug/mL). Plasma from six rats was used for the *ex vivo* study
(Methods, Pharmacokinetics study; Ex vivo antibacterial effect).

The bacterium was *S.* Typhimurium; the marbofloxacin MIC was 0.031 ug/mL for
the ATCC 14028 reference strain and field strain S-2, and 0.5 ug/mL for field
strain S-15 (Table 1).

```{r population}
str(uis[["Birhanu_2020_marbofloxacin_rat"]]$population, max.level = 1)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | MAR alone | MAR + MG | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL) | 1.0994 L/h/kg | 0.7291 L/h/kg | Table 3, CL (mL/h/kg) |
| `lvc` (V) | 5.986 L/kg | 4.1343 L/kg | Table 3, V (mL/kg) |
| `lka` (ka) | 7.6397 1/h | 1.0846 1/h | **Derived**: root of ln(ka/kel)/(ka - kel) = Tmax, Table 2 Tmax 0.5 / 2 h |
| `lfdepot` (F) | 1.31 | 0.891 | Results text, F = 131% / 89.1% |
| `e0` | 4.05 | 3.6 | Table 4, E0 |
| `limax` (Imax) | 10.86 | 10.66 | Table 4, Imax |
| `lic50` (IC50) | 405.99 h | 584.75 h | Table 4, IC50 (the Results text prints 504.8 for MAR + MG; see Errata) |
| `lhill` (gamma) | 5.41 | 10 | Table 4, Gamma |
| `mic` | 0.03125 ug/mL | 0.016 ug/mL | Table 1 (0.031, i.e. 1/32 ug/mL) / **derived** from Table 5 (see Part 3) |
| `log10_cfu0` | 6 | 6 | Methods, ex vivo inoculum 10^6 CFU/mL |
| `addSd`, `addSd_log_cfu` | 0 (fixed) | 0 (fixed) | Not reported |
| One-compartment disposition | | | Methods, Pharmacokinetics study; Table 3 |
| E = E0 - Imax Ce^gamma / (IC50^gamma + Ce^gamma) | | | Methods equation (sign corrected, see Errata); Figure 4 |
| Ce = C x 24 h / MIC | | | Methods, "Ce is the AUC0-24/MIC of the plasma"; Figure 4 x-axis |

# Part 1 - Marbofloxacin pharmacokinetics

```{r pk-sim}
grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.05), 0.25, 0.75)))
arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model, ~treatment, ~route, ~cmt,
  mods[1], "MAR", "IV", "central",
  mods[1], "MAR", "PO", "depot",
  mods[2], "MGM", "IV", "central",
  mods[2], "MGM", "PO", "depot"
)

sim_arm <- function(i) {
  a <- arms[i, ]
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = i, time = 0, amt = 5, evid = 1L, cmt = a$cmt),
    # Two declared endpoints (Cc and log_cfu): observation rows name the ODE
    # state and carry dvid = 1L, which returns both endpoint columns.
    data.frame(id = i, time = grid, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  )
  rxode2::rxSolve(readModelDb(a$model), events = ev, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = i, treatment = a$treatment, route = a$route)
}
pk_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), sim_arm))

stopifnot(
  nrow(pk_sim) == 4L * length(grid),
  all(is.finite(pk_sim$Cc)),
  all(is.finite(pk_sim$log_cfu))
)
```

## Closed-form checks against Tables 2 and 3

For a one-compartment model the intravenous `C0 = Dose/V` and `AUC = Dose/CL`,
the oral `AUC = F x Dose/CL`, and the oral `Cmax = (F x Dose/V) x exp(-kel x Tmax)`.
`Tmax` is reproduced by construction of `ka`; `Cmax` and both AUCs are not used
by any derivation and test the transcription.

```{r closed-form}
cf <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(mods, function(m) {
  th <- uis[[m]]$theta
  cl <- exp(th[["lcl"]])
  v <- exp(th[["lvc"]])
  ka <- exp(th[["lka"]])
  fb <- exp(th[["lfdepot"]])
  k <- cl / v
  tmax <- log(ka / k) / (ka - k)
  tibble::tibble(
    model = m,
    `IV C0 (ug/mL)` = 5 / v,
    `IV AUC (h*ug/mL)` = 5 / cl,
    `IV t1/2 (h)` = log(2) / k,
    `PO Tmax (h)` = tmax,
    `PO Cmax (ug/mL)` = fb * 5 / v * exp(-k * tmax),
    `PO AUC (h*ug/mL)` = fb * 5 / cl
  )
}))
pub_cf <- tibble::tibble(
  model = mods,
  `IV C0 (ug/mL)` = c(0.84, 1.21),
  `IV AUC (h*ug/mL)` = c(4.55, 6.86),
  `IV t1/2 (h)` = c(3.77, 3.93),
  `PO Tmax (h)` = c(0.5, 2),
  `PO Cmax (ug/mL)` = c(1.04, 0.78),
  `PO AUC (h*ug/mL)` = c(5.98, 6.11)
)
cf_long <- cf |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-model, names_to = "Quantity", values_to = "Model") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    pub_cf |> tidyr::pivot_longer(-model, names_to = "Quantity", values_to = "Published"),
    by = c("model", "Quantity")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(`% diff` = 100 * (Model / Published - 1))
knitr::kable(cf_long, digits = 3,
             caption = "Closed-form model quantities versus Birhanu 2020 Tables 2 and 3 (IV Cmax = C0).")

stopifnot(
  # Disposition reproduces the IV fit: values used to build the model.
  all(abs(cf_long$`% diff`[cf_long$Quantity %in% c("IV AUC (h*ug/mL)", "IV t1/2 (h)", "PO Tmax (h)")]) < 0.5),
  # Independent checks: the oral AUC and Cmax were never used to derive anything.
  all(abs(cf_long$`% diff`[cf_long$Quantity == "PO AUC (h*ug/mL)"]) < 1),
  all(abs(cf_long$`% diff`[cf_long$Quantity == "PO Cmax (ug/mL)"]) < 5)
)
```

The model's solved profile agrees with the closed form:

```{r ode-vs-closed-form}
cf_iv <- pk_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(route == "IV") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    v = ifelse(treatment == "MAR", exp(uis[[1]]$theta[["lvc"]]), exp(uis[[2]]$theta[["lvc"]])),
    cl = ifelse(treatment == "MAR", exp(uis[[1]]$theta[["lcl"]]), exp(uis[[2]]$theta[["lcl"]])),
    closed = 5 / v * exp(-cl / v * time)
  )
stopifnot(max(abs(cf_iv$Cc / cf_iv$closed - 1)) < 1e-6)
```

## Replicating Figure 2

```{r figure-2}
# Replicates Figure 2 of Birhanu 2020: panels A/B oral (semi-log, 0-12 h),
# panels C/D intravenous (linear, 0-24 h). Points are the means read from
# Figure 2 by the maintainers for orientation only; they are not fitted.
fig2_obs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~route, ~time, ~Cc,
  "MAR", "PO", 0.25, 0.32, "MAR", "PO", 0.5, 1.05, "MAR", "PO", 0.75, 0.93,
  "MAR", "PO", 1, 0.92, "MAR", "PO", 2, 0.58, "MAR", "PO", 4, 0.39,
  "MAR", "PO", 8, 0.26, "MAR", "PO", 12, 0.22,
  "MGM", "PO", 0.25, 0.43, "MGM", "PO", 0.5, 0.47, "MGM", "PO", 0.75, 0.53,
  "MGM", "PO", 1, 0.77, "MGM", "PO", 2, 0.78, "MGM", "PO", 4, 0.47,
  "MGM", "PO", 8, 0.26, "MGM", "PO", 12, 0.19,
  "MAR", "IV", 0.25, 1.55, "MAR", "IV", 0.5, 1.04, "MAR", "IV", 0.75, 0.79,
  "MAR", "IV", 1, 0.62, "MAR", "IV", 2, 0.45, "MAR", "IV", 4, 0.30,
  "MAR", "IV", 8, 0.21, "MAR", "IV", 12, 0.13,
  "MGM", "IV", 0.25, 1.94, "MGM", "IV", 0.5, 1.57, "MGM", "IV", 0.75, 1.25,
  "MGM", "IV", 1, 1.02, "MGM", "IV", 2, 0.80, "MGM", "IV", 4, 0.40,
  "MGM", "IV", 8, 0.27, "MGM", "IV", 12, 0.14
)

ggplot(pk_sim, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = fig2_obs, colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_grid(route ~ treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma marbofloxacin (ug/mL)",
       title = "Figure 2 - marbofloxacin after 5 mg/kg",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Birhanu 2020. Line: packaged model; points: figure means.")
```

The intravenous lines are the authors' own one-compartment fits, which, like
the published Figure 2C/D curves, underpredict the first samples: the data are
visibly biexponential but only a one-compartment fit was reported. The oral terminal phase in Figure 2A/B is flatter than the
intravenous one, which is why the oral non-compartmental half-lives (7.62 and
6.01 h) exceed the intravenous ones (3.77 and 3.93 h); the model carries the
intravenous disposition for both routes.

## PKNCA validation against Tables 2 and 3

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- pk_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(group = paste(treatment, route)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, group)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | group + id)
dose_df <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, group) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 5)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | group + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 24,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

```{r nca-compare}
# Birhanu 2020 Table 2 (oral; AUCall, HL_Lambda_z) and Table 3 (IV; AUC,
# K10_HL, Cmax). The IV AUC of Table 3 is the model-fit AUC to infinity,
# compared here with AUC0-24, which is 98% of it.
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~auclast, ~half.life,
  "MAR PO", 1.04, 0.5, 5.98, 7.62,
  "MGM PO", 0.78, 2, 6.11, 6.01,
  "MAR IV", 0.84, NA, 4.55, 3.77,
  "MGM IV", 1.21, NA, 6.86, 3.93
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "group",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", tmax = "h", auclast = "h*ug/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated versus Birhanu 2020 Tables 2 and 3. * differs by >20%.")
```

The two starred rows are the oral half-lives, explained under Figure 2. Every
other row is within the tolerance.

# Part 2 - Ex vivo antibacterial effect

## Replicating Figure 4

The *ex vivo* effect is a function of the sample's index only, so the curves can
be drawn directly from the packaged parameters.

```{r figure-4}
pd_par <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(mods, function(m) {
  th <- uis[[m]]$theta
  tibble::tibble(
    model = m,
    treatment = ifelse(m == mods[1], "MAR", "MGM"),
    e0 = th[["e0"]], imax = exp(th[["limax"]]), ic50 = exp(th[["lic50"]]),
    hill = exp(th[["lhill"]]), mic = th[["mic"]]
  )
}))
effect_of <- function(ce, p) p$e0 - p$imax * ce^p$hill / (ce^p$hill + p$ic50^p$hill)

fig4 <- tidyr::crossing(pd_par, ce = seq(0, 1200, by = 5)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(E = e0 - imax * ce^hill / (ce^hill + ic50^hill))

ggplot(fig4, aes(ce, E)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(x = "AUC/MIC 0-24 (h)", y = "Effect (log10 CFU/mL)",
       title = "Figure 4 - ex vivo sigmoid Imax model",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Birhanu 2020.")
```

Both curves start at `e0` (+4.05 and +3.6) and fall to `e0 - imax` (-6.81 and
-7.06), as in Figure 4A/B. The equation printed in the Methods has a `+` in
front of `Imax`, which would make the effect *rise* to +14.9; Figure 4 shows
the fall, so the packaged models use the minus sign.

## The packaged model's ex vivo output

`log_cfu` is the predicted count after 24 h of incubation of a plasma sample
drawn at the current time. Its value at the sampling times of Figure 3 is
shown below, together with the windows the paper reports.

```{r exvivo-windows}
draws <- c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24)
win <- pk_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(route == "PO", time %in% draws) |>
  dplyr::mutate(E = log_cfu - 6) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, time, Cc, log_cfu, E)
knitr::kable(
  win |> tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = time, names_from = treatment, values_from = E) |>
    dplyr::rename(`Draw time (h)` = time, `MAR alone: E (log10)` = MAR, `MAR + MG: E (log10)` = MGM),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Predicted 24 h ex vivo change for plasma drawn after oral dosing (negative = inhibition)."
)

stopifnot(
  # The output is log10_cfu0 + E exactly, with E bounded by e0 and e0 - imax.
  all(win$log_cfu <= 6 + max(pd_par$e0) + 1e-8),
  all(win$log_cfu >= 6 + min(pd_par$e0 - pd_par$imax) - 1e-8)
)
```

Birhanu 2020 reports inhibition for plasma drawn from 0.25 to 2 h after oral MAR
alone and from 0.25 to 4 h with MG. The model inhibits from 0.25 to 4 h for MAR
alone and from 0.5 to 4 h with MG. The packaged PK is the mean intravenous fit
of ten rats with a reconstructed oral input, whereas the *ex vivo* plasma came
from six rats, so a one-sample shift at either edge is expected; the windows
were not used to set any parameter.

# Part 3 - PK/PD indices and dosages (Table 5)

## The MIC behind each index

Table 5 prints the indices from the oral Table 2 values. For MAR alone they
follow from the Table 1 MIC; for MAR + MG they require an MIC of 0.016 ug/mL,
which the paper never states.

```{r indices}
idx <- tibble::tibble(
  treatment = c("MAR", "MGM"),
  auc = c(5.98, 6.11), cmax = c(1.04, 0.78),
  `AUC24/MIC published` = c(191.22, 381.93),
  `Cmax/MIC published` = c(33.39, 49.06),
  mic = pd_par$mic
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `AUC24/MIC with model mic` = auc / mic,
    `Cmax/MIC with model mic` = cmax / mic,
    `AUC24/MIC with MIC 0.031` = auc / 0.031,
    `AUC24/MIC with MIC 0.008` = auc / 0.008
  )
knitr::kable(idx |> dplyr::mutate(mic = format(mic)), digits = 2,
             caption = "Table 5 indices reconstructed from Table 2 means (mic in ug/mL).")

stopifnot(
  abs(idx$`AUC24/MIC with model mic` / idx$`AUC24/MIC published` - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(idx$`Cmax/MIC with model mic` / idx$`Cmax/MIC published` - 1) < 0.02
)
```

The same 0.016 ug/mL places the largest MAR + MG plasma sample of Figure 4B
(about 0.78 ug/mL) at `r sprintf("%.0f", 0.78 * 24 / 0.016)` h on the x-axis,
where the figure's last points sit; the checkerboard combination value of
0.008 ug/mL would place it beyond 2300 h.

## Dosages

Birhanu 2020 computes the dose for each endpoint as
`Dose = (AUC/MIC) x CL x MIC / (fu x F)`. The three targets are the indices at
which the fitted Imax curve gives a 24 h change of 0 (bacteriostatic), -3
(bactericidal) and -4 log10 (bacterial elimination). The published dosages are
reproduced exactly with `fu = 1`, the oral `CL/F` from Table 2 and the oral `F`,
using an MIC of 0.03125 ug/mL for MAR alone and **0.008 ug/mL** for MAR + MG.

```{r dosages}
index_for <- function(target, p) {
  fr <- (p$e0 - target) / p$imax
  p$ic50 * (fr / (1 - fr))^(1 / p$hill)
}
dose_tab <- tidyr::crossing(pd_par, target = c(0, -3, -4)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(treatment, dplyr::desc(target)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    index = index_for(target, list(e0 = e0, imax = imax, ic50 = ic50, hill = hill)),
    clf = ifelse(treatment == "MAR", 0.70542, 0.75398), # Table 2 Cl_F_obs (L/h/kg)
    fbio = ifelse(treatment == "MAR", 1.31, 0.891), # Results text
    mic_dose = ifelse(treatment == "MAR", 0.03125, 0.008),
    `Dose, reconstructed` = index * mic_dose * clf / fbio,
    `Dose, model mic` = index * mic * clf / fbio,
    `Dose, Table 5` = c(6.20, 7.65, 8.3, 3.70, 4.16, 4.34)[match(paste(treatment, target),
      paste(rep(c("MAR", "MGM"), each = 3), rep(c(0, -3, -4), 2)))]
  )
knitr::kable(
  dose_tab |>
    dplyr::select(treatment, target, index, mic_dose, `Dose, reconstructed`, `Dose, Table 5`, `Dose, model mic`) |>
    dplyr::mutate(mic_dose = format(mic_dose)) |>
    dplyr::rename(Treatment = treatment, `Target E (log10)` = target, `Index (h)` = index,
                  `MIC used (ug/mL)` = mic_dose),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Table 5 dosages reconstructed from the packaged Table 4 parameters."
)

stopifnot(max(abs(dose_tab$`Dose, reconstructed` - dose_tab$`Dose, Table 5`)) < 0.011)
```

This check pins every Table 4 parameter: with the Results-text IC50 of 504.8
for MAR + MG the three dosages would be
`r paste(sprintf("%.2f", vapply(c(0, -3, -4), function(t) index_for(t, dplyr::mutate(pd_par[2, ], ic50 = 504.8)) * 0.008 * 0.75398 / 0.891, numeric(1))), collapse = ", ")`
mg/kg instead of 3.70, 4.16 and 4.34, and with a plus sign in the Imax
equation no negative target could be reached at all.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Oral absorption is reconstructed.** Birhanu 2020 analysed the oral data
  non-compartmentally and published no absorption rate constant. `ka` is the
  root of the one-compartment `Tmax` identity at the published `Tmax`, with the
  intravenous `kel`; `F` is the published bioavailability. The oral `Cmax` and
  AUC, which were not used, are reproduced within about 4% and 0.4%.
- **The oral terminal half-life is not reproduced.** The model gives the
  intravenous half-life (3.77 and 3.93 h) for both routes; the oral
  non-compartmental values are 7.62 and 6.01 h. A single disposition cannot carry
  both, and the authors' fitted model is the intravenous one.
- **Bioavailability above 100%.** The published `F` for MAR alone is 131%
  (oral AUC 5.98 over intravenous AUC 4.55 h\*ug/mL). It is kept as printed; it
  is a ratio of separately averaged crossover arms, not a physical fraction.
- **Methyl gallate is not modelled.** It was not quantifiable in plasma. The
  combination file describes marbofloxacin when MG 20 mg/kg is co-administered
  by the same route, and its *ex vivo* parameters describe the combined activity
  of that plasma.
- **Ex vivo index.** A plasma sample is incubated at its fixed concentration, so
  its AUC0-24 is `C x 24 h`. The paper's index uses the undiluted plasma
  concentration (the Figure 4 axes match it), not the 1:10 in-well
  concentration. The sigmoid parameters were fitted to plasma from orally dosed
  rats; the packaged models apply the same concentration-effect relation after
  either route.
- **MIC values.** MAR alone uses 0.03125 ug/mL, the twofold-dilution value
  printed as 0.031; it reproduces the Table 5 dosages (0.031 gives 6.16 rather
  than 6.20 mg/kg). MAR + MG uses 0.016 ug/mL, derived from Table 5 and
  Figure 4B as shown in Part 3.
- **No variability.** The `+/-` values are standard deviations of per-rat
  estimates, not variance components, so there are no `eta` terms and both
  residual SDs are fixed at zero.

# Errata

- **Sign of the Imax equation.** The Methods print
  `E = E0 + Imax x Ce^gamma / (IC50^gamma + Ce^gamma)`. Figure 4 and the Table 5
  dosages both require `E0 - Imax x ...`; the models use the minus sign.
- **IC50 for MAR + MG.** The Results text gives 504.8; Table 4 gives 584.75.
  Figure 4B and the Table 5 dosages confirm 584.75, which is used.
- **The MAR + MG dosages use a different MIC from the MAR + MG index.** The
  Table 5 indices and Figure 4B are built on an MIC of 0.016 ug/mL, but the
  Table 5 dosages are reproduced only with 0.008 ug/mL, the marbofloxacin
  concentration in the checkerboard combination (Table 1 text). With the
  0.016 ug/mL that defines the fitted IC50, the same equation gives
  `r paste(sprintf("%.2f", dose_tab[["Dose, model mic"]][dose_tab$treatment == "MGM"]), collapse = ", ")`
  mg/kg for MAR + MG, so the reported 40% dose reduction from the
  combination depends on mixing the two MICs.
- **Small transcription differences.** The abstract gives AUC24/MIC 192.8 and
  intravenous AUC 4.54 h\*ug/mL for MAR alone; Tables 3 and 5 give 191.22 and
  4.55. The tables are used. Table 3 labels its `K10` as 0.18 1/h for both arms;
  the printed `CL` and `V` give 0.184 and 0.176 1/h, consistent with the printed
  half-lives and MRTs.
- No erratum or correction notice for this article was found in Europe PMC as
  of 2026-11-27.
